newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela oil firm launches anti-strike measures.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela oil firm launches anti-strike measures.

text.p: Venezuela's state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) will launch its contingency plan this afternoon to prepare for a 12-hour strike due to start on Wednesday at 0600 local time/1000 GMT, a spokeswoman said Tuesday.
The general strike was called by Venezuela's largest trade union, the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), to protest at the private sector's failure to raise salaries.
"Professional workers will assume the operations in place of workers who go on strike. In this way we will guarantee continued operations," the PDVSA spokeswoman said.
She said production, refining and marketing of the country's 3.2 million barrel per day oil production would not be interrupted by the strike.
Carlos Ortega, president of the largest oil workers' union Fedepetrol, said last week some 60,000 oil workers would participate in the nationwide action.
In previous strikes, PDVSA has successfully avoided any disruption in its operations using senior employees to replace workers.
